chain.label: Operator's inadequate tire maintenance practices
chain.trigger: the operator's inadequate maintenance of the airplane's tires, which resulted in multiple tire failures during takeoff roll due to severe underinflation

chain.label: Learjet thrust reverser / wheel-well design deficiency inadequately certified
chain.trigger: deficiencies in Learjet's design of and the Federal Aviation Administration's certification of the Learjet Model 60's thrust reverser system, which permitted the failure of critical systems in the wheel well area to result in uncommanded forward thrust

chain.label: Inadequate industry/flight-crew training for tire failure events
chain.trigger: inadequate industry training standards for flight crews in tire failure scenarios

chain.label: Poor crew resource management by the flight crew
chain.trigger: the flight crew's poor crew resource management (CRM)

chain.label: Severe underinflation of all four MLG tires (~36%)
chain.trigger: all four MLG tires on the airplane were operating while severely underinflated during the takeoff roll, which resulted in the tire failures

caused_by.evidence: the accident airplane's insufficient tire air pressure was due to Global Exec Aviation's inadequate maintenance

chain.label: Sequential failure of all four main landing gear tires during takeoff roll
chain.trigger: the CVR captured the beginning of a loud rumbling sound ... debris evidence showed that ... all of the MLG tires had failed

caused_by.evidence: severely underinflated ... which resulted in the tire failures

chain.label: Captain's decision to reject the takeoff after V1
chain.trigger: the captain's execution of a rejected takeoff (RTO) after V1, which was inconsistent with her training and standard operating procedures

caused_by.evidence: the onset of the loud rumbling noise likely resulted from pieces of the right outboard tire separating from the wheel and striking the underside of the airplane
the accident pilots would have been better prepared to recognize the tire failure and to continue the takeoff if they had received realistic training
the captain's indecision in responding to the anomaly and her failure to follow standard operating procedures was the result of a combination of poor CRM skills

chain.label: Tire debris damage to squat switch/wiring causing loss of ground-mode signal
chain.trigger: the circuit associated with the MLG electrical components and wiring, which include the wheel speed sensor and squat switch, must have sustained damage that affected the air-ground signal

caused_by.evidence: debris found on the runway and other physical evidence show that the MLG area where system components were mounted sustained damage from the shedding tire fragments
two hydraulic lines in each wheel well of the Learjet 60 did not have the protection of a restrictor, making it possible to lose the hydraulic supply if those tubes were breached

chain.label: Uncommanded thrust reverser stowage producing uncommanded forward thrust
chain.trigger: the EECs shifted logic and signaled the FADEC components to change to the forward thrust power schedule ... signaled the FADEC components to provide forward thrust at near takeoff power

caused_by.evidence: because the system logic requirements for maintaining thrust reverser deployment were no longer being met, the thrust reversers stowed
deficiencies in Learjet's design ... permitted the failure of critical systems in the wheel well area to result in uncommanded forward thrust

chain.label: Runway overrun off the departure end of runway 11
chain.trigger: the airplane ... overran runway 11 during a rejected takeoff

caused_by.evidence: the captain's action to reject the takeoff after the airplane had passed V1 placed the flight crew and passengers in a high-risk situation; accident and incident data show that high-speed RTOs can result in runway overruns
the accident airplane's uncommanded forward thrust ... substantially increased the airplane's runway excursion speed

chain.label: Impact with terrain, obstacles, and highway embankment beyond the runway
chain.trigger: the airplane passed through the 1,000-foot runway safety area (RSA), struck airport lighting and navigation antennas, and descended a steep downhill slope before striking a lighting pole and the perimeter fence

caused_by.evidence: the controller observed that the airplane went straight off the end of the runway

chain.label: Fatal and serious injuries to occupants; postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The captain, the first officer, and two passengers were killed; two other passengers were seriously injured

caused_by.evidence: the airplane stopped and exploded into a fireball; the cause of death for both the captain and the first officer was reported as smoke and fume inhalation and thermal injuries
